body:
Please leave your feedback about new 'mini.move' module here. Feel free to either add new comment or positively upvote existing one.

Some things I am interested to find out (obviously, besides bugs):

- Are configuration and function names intuitive enough?
- Are default values of settings convenient for you?
- Is documentation and examples clear enough?

Thanks!

comment_data.body:
Hello Evgeni!
Awesome work as usual!
Function names and documentation were pretty clear for me.

**Some issues:**
1. Sometimes when I'm moveing lines vertically lines "jumble" or shake a bit (tried recording it with asciinema and into a gif but it's too fast for them, lmk if you need a showcase and ill see what I can do).
My guess would be that I'm seeing the split second between the 'cut' and 'paste' actions, maybe swapping lines with `nvim_buf_set_lines()` fixes it.

1. The same "jumbling" happens when holding down the keys (activating keyboard auto repeat) trying to move one or more lines into the buffers top or bottom edges, I suspect this is the same as `#1` but I'll list it just to be sure.

**A Request:**
1. Moving lines over folds is handled nicely, however moving folds themselves happens only once and they get opened, I've always wanted to see this feature but I haven't seen any moving plugin that does it.

> **Some issues:**
> 
>     1. Sometimes when I'm moveing lines vertically lines "jumble" or shake a bit (tried recording it with asciinema and into a gif but it's too fast for them, lmk if you need a showcase and ill see what I can do).
>        My guess would be that I'm seeing the split second between the 'cut' and 'paste' actions, maybe swapping lines with `nvim_buf_set_lines()` fixes it.
> 
>     2. The same "jumbling" happens when holding down the keys (activating keyboard auto repeat) trying to move one or more lines into the buffers top or bottom edges, I suspect this is the same as `#1` but I'll list it just to be sure.

Unfortunately, I can't replicate any of these two. For me it is as smooth as moving cursor. I don't think redraw should happen between "cut" and "paste" (not 100% sure, though). 

One thing I noticed when trying to replicate the second point is that lines were reformatted and automatically collapsed into a fold (I have `foldmethod=indent`), but on the next step it again was reformatted outside of fold. The fold creation lead to line collapsing which indeed look like a glitch of some sort.

Another possible source of the issue might be tree-sitter highlighting and diagnostic. Could you try this in regular buffer without highlight and diagnostic, and see if it still there?

> **A Request:**
> 
>     1. Moving lines over folds is handled nicely, however moving folds themselves happens only ones and they get opened, I've always wanted to see this feature but I haven't seen any moving plugin that does it.

That is a **great** suggestion. My first instinct is that there is no such functionality for a reason: folds are usually created automatically by method from `:h 'foldmethod'`. They seem to be managed "from outside" only in case of `foldmethod=manual`, which is not ideal.

So this is a "I would love to do this, but I don't know how and if it is even possible" case.

> Another possible source of the issue ...

I've disabled treesitter entirely and it's still jittering, I've [captured](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/16624558/212563701-7cad100d-d309-416c-b35e-1416a9a18b92.mp4) it with obs

I might try the buffer line swap `nvim_buf_set_lines()` implementation on my end and report back.

> My first instinct is that there is no such functionality for a reason ...

Plugin authors in general steer away from fold manipulation because nvim doesn't provide an API for querying them [yet](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/19226).

I've implemented a very crude `nvim_buf_set_lines()` solution (linewise and vertical only) I was talking about earlier.
It lacks many of the niceties currently present but the jittering is gone. lmk what you think.

```lua
MiniMove.move_line = function(direction)
  if H.is_disabled() then return end

  local cmd = function(x) vim.cmd('normal!' .. x) end

  local lnr = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)[1]

  if direction == 'up' then
    local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, lnr-2, lnr, true)
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, lnr-2, lnr, true, {lines[2], lines[1]})
    cmd 'k'
  elseif direction == 'down' then
    local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, lnr-1, lnr+1, true)
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, lnr-1, lnr+1, true, {lines[2], lines[1]})
    cmd 'j'
  end
end
```

I have just pushed some updates. Among fixes, there are two relatively small, but significant features:
- Cursor now moves along the linewise selection. This is indeed more intuitive. Thanks @davidsierradz!
- There is now a `config.options` field controlling movement. It now has the `reindent_linewise` option, which can be used to disable automatic reindent when moving linewise. What does `nmap K` says? It should be something having `MiniMove` in it. If not, find the place in your config files where it is mapped and don't map it.

It is a common choice for `vim.lsp.buf.hover`, so maybe that is it. It is used in default `on_attach` in 'nvim-lspconfig'.

Good call, I assumed that since it was last in the config it'd take precedence, but apparently not, most likely due to the on_attach event.

```
:nmap K
n  K           *@<Lua 807: /usr/local/Cellar/neovim/0.8.1/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/buf.lua:41>
                 Hover
n  K           * <Cmd>lua MiniMove.move_line('up')<CR>
                 Move line up
```

And sure enough, commenting out the following from the lspconfig on_attach function from the [docs](https://github.com/neovim/nvim-lspconfig) makes the `K` mapping work. 

```lua
vim.keymap.set("n", "K", vim.lsp.buf.hover, bufopts)
```

Maybe it is worth putting in the help page as the lspconfig is a quite popular package.

`MiniMove.move_line()` is designed to be used in Normal mode. Replace `mode = 'v'` with `mode = 'n'` and it should work.

Also, there is no need to supply `opts` to 'mini.move' functions. In your case `opts` is a config for `setup()` telling it to not create mappings. Options for both `move_selection()` and `move_line()` have the same structure as `config.options`. Right now it can be used to not reindent during linewise movement.

@echasnovski Thanks alot! Works nicely now.

One nitpick, which could also go into documentation as it creates some complexity to handle interval logic: using `:set ve=all` creates empty lines which are not truncated.

I did also find, that spaces <-> tabs conversion might lead to surprising behavior on line movement:
https://asciinema.org/a/vU5F0KlQMcDDwIGQF1VKImX3Q

Both things could/should be probably documented in a FAQ.

> One nitpick, which could also go into documentation as it creates some complexity to handle interval logic: using :set ve=all creates empty lines which are not truncated.

It is not because of `virtualedit=all` but because moving selection *only moves selection* and does nothing more. If you make a selection at the end of line with only whitespace to the left, it will move that selection leaving trailing whitespace untouched. In your case of `ve=all` you probably make intermediate moves creating this type of lines, which when moved further recreate this situation. Usage of `[count]` might prevent that.

Here is a demo (lines 3 and 4 are empty):

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24854248/216561917-bc357571-46f1-4091-b86b-b57d814b6096.mp4

This is a natural consequence of moving selection which just happens to be prepended by whitespace instead of other characters, so not sure if it deserves separate mention in help file.

> I did also find, that spaces <-> tabs conversion might lead to surprising behavior on line movement:

I am not sure what you think is surprising here. By default, [vertical linewise movement is reindented with `=`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/8e007cf3ae8db59bd926a9fbaf7f0d25a7fe67ca/doc/mini-move.txt#L15). This is the effect I see here. As it doesn't always play nice with what user wants, there is an [option to disable it](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/8e007cf3ae8db59bd926a9fbaf7f0d25a7fe67ca/doc/mini-move.txt#L103-L104). Use it like this:

```lua
require('mini.move').setup({ options = { reindent_linewise = false } })
```
The 'mini.move' is now out of beta-testing after the release of version 0.7.0. Thank you all for your input!
